blocks.text: Lincoln Park Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Lincoln Park is an established residential neighbourhood on Port Coquitlam's north side, around Lincoln Avenue and Lincoln Drive, Laurier Avenue and Coast Meridian Road, with Fraser Avenue at its south side; the City publishes no street-by-street boundary for this sub-area, so treat street limits as a working orientation, not an official line.

The City's Official Community Plan (OCP) groups Lincoln Park with Mary Hill as established residential neighbourhoods which developed from the 1950s onwards, distinct from the newer Riverwood and Citadel areas.
Hyde Creek runs through the neighbourhood's east side: the City lists Hyde Creek Nature Reserve at 1457 Lincoln Drive, inside the street pattern the houses front.

blocks.text: Lincoln Park Houses: the housing stock

items.t: The subdivision floor for the main house zones is set city-wide in Zoning Bylaw No. 3630; Lincoln Park lots are checked against those Residential Small-Scale zone minimums lot by lot.

In-area anchors are the two School District No. 43 (Coquitlam) schools inside the streets: Birchland Elementary at 1331 Fraser Avenue and Minnekhada Middle School at 1390 Laurier Avenue, with Hyde Creek Recreation Centre at 1379 Laurier Avenue between them on the same street as the middle school.

blocks.text: Lincoln Park Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: City-wide rules — Zoning Bylaw, 2008, No. 3630, small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH), the OCP Bylaw, 2013, No. 3838 and the 2026 tax and utility figures — are covered in full in the Mary Hill Port Coquitlam houses-for-sale guide; this section covers the Lincoln Park-specific checks.

Work near Hyde Creek or another watercourse, ditch or adjacent environmentally sensitive land in a designated area needs a Watercourse Development Permit, or a City-confirmed exemption, before filling, clearing vegetation, paving or building — the first permit check for a Lincoln Drive or Laurier Avenue lot backing onto the creek corridor.

The OCP designates Transit-Oriented Areas (TOAs) in Port Coquitlam, including lands adjacent to the Lincoln SkyTrain Station across the Coquitlam border, with prescribed residential density and height tiers — relevant context for the west edge of this neighbourhood closest to that station, with the tier map in the OCP itself.

blocks.text: Lincoln Park Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Hyde Creek Nature Reserve at 1457 Lincoln Drive covers 539,110 square metres with walking trails, per the City's parks directory — the largest single green space inside this house pocket, and the reason Lincoln Drive's east side fronts forest and creek, not more houses.

Waste collection is by zone, not by neighbourhood name: Port Coquitlam has five collection zones, green carts are weekly, and blue recycling and grey garbage carts alternate weeks, so a Lincoln Park address must be looked up on the zone map.
Route 173, Cedar to Coquitlam Central Station, runs the neighbourhood's west and north edges via Coast Meridian Road, Coquitlam Avenue and Oxford Street, through Port Coquitlam Station.

Route 174, Rocklin to Coquitlam Central Station, runs via Coast Meridian Road, Greenmount Avenue, Wellington Street, Mason Street and Oxford Street, and continues as the 173 at its Victoria Drive terminus.

Port Coquitlam Station is the neighbourhood's West Coast Express stop: TransLink lists its park-and-ride at 267 spaces, open 7 days a week, 4 a.m. to 2 a.m., at a $3 daily and $60 monthly rate, and the West Coast Express runs weekdays only, with no weekend or statutory-holiday service.

blocks.text: Lincoln Park Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the City's flood-watch history for the creek and park edge: a City notice closed Birchland Park during a high-water event while crews monitored drainage systems, culverts and pump stations, which is the documented behaviour of this neighbourhood's low ground.

Check watercourse rules before altering a creek-side lot: filling, clearing vegetation, paving or building near a watercourse, ditch or adjacent environmentally sensitive land in a designated area needs a Watercourse Development Permit or a City-confirmed exemption.

Check tree rules before clearing: Tree Bylaw, 2019, No. 4108 regulates tree removal, and a tree cutting permit can be refused during the active bird nesting season unless a biological survey by a qualified environmental professional is submitted.

blocks.text: Between Oxford Heights and Riverwood in northeast Port Coquitlam, Lincoln Park is an established neighbourhood. Single-family houses and townhomes line its quiet streets, and Terry Fox Secondary serves the north side. With Fremont Village shopping and the Coast Meridian Overpass close by, it’s a good fit for families planning to stay put.
Lincoln Park home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

13 houses sold in Lincoln Park with a median price of $1,290,000 (the middle half sold between $1,165,000 and $1,400,000), taking a median of 34 days to sell at 97.9% of the last list price; 8% sold above list. They had a median $576 per square foot, a median year built of 1975 and a median lot of 6,000 square feet.

faq.a: The Greater Vancouver REALTORS® counted 12 houses listed in Lincoln Park at the end of October 2026. The number changes daily, so ask Jared for today’s count.
faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Lincoln Park?

faq.a: With a sales ratio of 25% in October 2026, houses in Lincoln Park sat in a sellers’ market. The reports read under 12% as a buyers’ market and over 20% as a sellers’ market.
faq.q: Is Lincoln Park a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?

faq.a: Between June and October 2026, 8 houses sold in Lincoln Park; Port Coquitlam as a whole recorded 91.
faq.q: How many houses sold in Lincoln Park from June to October 2026?

faq.a: Two School District No. 43 schools sit inside the neighbourhood: Birchland Elementary at 1331 Fraser Avenue for kindergarten to Grade 5, and Minnekhada Middle School at 1390 Laurier Avenue for Grades 6 to 8. No secondary school sits inside the sub-area.
faq.q: Which schools are physically inside Lincoln Park?

faq.a: The City lists Hyde Creek Recreation Centre at 1379 Laurier Avenue, eleven numbers from Minnekhada Middle School on the same street, with pool, fitness, children and youth programs and racquet courts in the City's Fall 2026 Leisure Guide, open Monday to Friday 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. and Saturday and Sunday 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. It is this neighbourhood's own recreation centre, not a downtown facility.
faq.q: What is at Hyde Creek Recreation Centre, and where exactly is it?

faq.a: Flood status is per property here, not per neighbourhood. Check the specific lot on the City flood page rather than assuming the north-side streets are all clear.
faq.q: Is Lincoln Park in the floodplain?

faq.a: TransLink routes 173 and 174 are the neighbourhood's pair, and each continues as the other. Route 173 runs via Coast Meridian Road, Coquitlam Avenue and Oxford Street, and route 174 runs via Coast Meridian Road, Greenmount Avenue, Wellington Street and Oxford Street, both linking Port Coquitlam Station with Coquitlam Central Station.
